subject: Reranker integration discovery & evaluation next steps
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@searchlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Reranker integration discovery & evaluation next steps

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — really helpful context. I wanted to capture the technical follow-ups and proposed next steps so our teams can move quickly on a pilot. Below is a short recap plus specific asks on the integration and evaluation side.

Quick recap of requirements we heard
- Use case: search relevance re-ranking for personalized results across web + mobile.
- Traffic: a few hundred qps during peak, mostly short queries (avg 12 tokens).
- Security: must support customer-managed keying and audit logs for the pilot.

Technical follow-ups / questions for your engineering team (please share artifacts where possible)
1) SDK & auth
   - Do you prefer Redwood SDK (we provide a client), or do you want to call our HTTP endpoints directly?
   - Authentication: service-to-service OAuth2 vs API keys vs mTLS/JWT — which is required on your side?
2) Routing & throughput
   - Will requests be routed by customer id? Do you need prefix routing or per-tenant model pinning?
   - Expected concurrency and acceptable tail latency (p95/p99).
3) Structured output / tool calling
   - Any planned use of structured tool outputs (e.g., JSON with fields to hydrate the UI)? If yes, what schema?
4) Embeddings & candidate generation
   - Do you surface dense candidates from an ANN store? If so, what vector dim and approximate indexing latency?
5) Reranker evaluation & metrics (critical)
   - Can you provide a small labeled seed (50–500 queries) with graded relevance so we can run an offline eval?
   - Target metrics you care about (examples: MRR, NDCG@10, precision@k, recall@k, hit-rate). Please indicate current baseline values if available.
   - Do you want us to recommend an initial top_k to re-rank (we commonly start with top_k = 10 or 20 depending on candidate generation recall)?

Proposed immediate next steps
- You: share a small labeled seed and an architecture diagram (attachments ok).
- Us: prepare a one-hour integration workshop to walk SDK/auth and run a dry-run offline eval on the seed.
- Joint: agree on evaluation rubric and success criteria for a 2-week pilot (offline -> canary -> production rollout).

Please let me know if I missed anything and share times that work for a technical workshop (I can do Thu/Fri afternoon PST this week).

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Maya — thanks for the clear note and the plan. Happy to move forward. Answers inline below + attaching a small seed and our system diagram.

1) SDK & auth- We can accept either HTTP calls or your SDK; engineering prefers using Redwood's SDK for faster onboarding.
- Auth: service-to-service OAuth2 JWT (we have a short-lived token flow). API keys are discouraged here.

2) Routing & throughput- Requests are routed by customer_id header. We expect peak ~250 qps with spikes; p95 target < 150ms and p99 < 350ms for re-rank step.

3) Structured output / tool calling- We will consume structured JSON from the reranker that includes {candidate_id, score, rationale_html}. Schema attached in doc.

4) Embeddings & candidate generation- Dense candidates from a FAISS-ish store, dim=768, average retrieval latency ~35ms. We will send candidate lists (ids + vectors) to the reranker.

5) Reranker evaluation & metrics- Attached: searchlytics_relevance_seed.csv (200 queries, graded relevance 0/1/2), and searchlytics_system_arch.vsdx. Current baseline on their internal scoring: MRR=0.42, NDCG@10=0.57, precision@5=0.48.
- We are comfortable starting with top_k=20 for offline tuning, but would be open to trying top_k=10 for latency-conscious canaries.

Workshop times: Thu 2026-07-22 10:00am PDT or Fri 2026-07-23 9:00am PDT — either works for us.

Attachments: searchlytics_relevance_seed.csv; searchlytics_system_arch.vsdx (zip: small diagram)

—Oliver

Nice summary, Maya — a couple quick internal notes before the workshop: 

- We should schedule a 60–90m integration workshop and include one of our runtime engineers (I'll add Rajesh). Agenda: SDK setup, auth flow demo (OAuth2 JWT exchange), sample request/response with structured output, and how we expect candidate lists to be formatted.
- Recommend we propose a dedicated routing key header: X-Redwood-Tenant (customer_id) so we can pin model variants per tenant in Dedicated mode if they spin that up later.
- For the offline eval, we'll run MRR, NDCG@10, precision@5 and precision@10. Also recommend logging token_count and per-request latency for cost analysis.

Great — thanks Oliver and Ben. Confirming the plan and a few clarifications before the workshop: 

1) Workshop time: Fri 2026-07-23 09:00am PDT (we'll run 60 minutes). Ben will add Rajesh from runtime.
2) Auth: we'll demo the OAuth2 JWT exchange and provide a short script to mint tokens from your service account.
3) Offline eval plan:
   - Redwood will run the first pass offline on your seed (top_k = 20 as you suggested) and report MRR, NDCG@10, precision@5, precision@10.
   - For the canary, we recommend trimming to top_k = 10 to meet p95 latency targets; we'll provide a tradeoff chart after the offline run.
4) Logging & instrumentation (please ensure these fields are emitted in pilot logs):
   - query_id, candidate_ids (order preserved), relevance_label (if available), reranker_score, request_latency_ms, token_count, model_version
5) Success criteria (suggested): delta MRR >= +0.05 and p95 latency <= 180ms for canary traffic. We can adjust.

Please confirm you received the attachments and the 09:00am PDT slot. If all good, Ben/Rajesh will send the workshop calendar invite with a Zoom link and our short pre-work checklist.

Cheers,
